fixes.explanation: The synagogues, friend. Verse 20 says Saul promptly began to proclaim Jesus there. He went where the community gathered and said it out loud. Most of us need three practice runs just to order at a drive-through.

The city gates do show up in this story, just not here. Acts 9:24 says people watched them day and night. Saul's preaching in verse 20 happens in the synagogues. Right city, and an easy one to mix up.
Those are Saul's words, and they're big ones: “He is the Son of God.” Saul wasn't just saying nice things about Jesus. He was saying who Jesus is. I'd say that's pretty bold, wouldn't you?
Astounded is the word in verse 21. Hearing Saul preach Jesus knocked them sideways. They even start asking questions about it. I'd be asking questions too, and I'd be holding my hat.
Nobody who heard him was unmoved, friend. Verse 21 says all who heard him were astounded. Astounded is about as far from unmoved as you can get. I'm betting nobody checked their watch.

Verse 22 says he confounded them by proving that Jesus is the Christ. The text gives Saul's proving as the way he did it. The Jews living in Damascus were confounded. I know that feeling, mostly from group chats.

A sign in the street would make a great scene, but the text doesn't show one. Verse 22 says Saul confounded the Jews living in Damascus by proving that Jesus is the Christ. His proving is how he did it. No fireworks, just a man who was empowered all the more.

A merchant's cart isn't in the text, friend. The gates were being watched day and night. Verse 25 has a different way out: his disciples took Saul and lowered him in a basket through a window in the wall.
Verse 26 says they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple. I think that was a hard door to knock on. Saul tried to join them, and fear is what he met.
A warm welcome would be nice, but that isn't what happens. Verse 26 says they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple. Then Barnabas shows up in verse 27.
The apostles, friend. Verse 27 says Barnabas, a Levite from Cyprus (Acts 4:36), brought Saul to them. Then Barnabas told them how Saul had seen the Lord. I think that was a kind thing to do.

Priests are in this story, just not here. In Damascus, the people who heard Saul asked whether he had come to take those who call on Jesus' name as prisoners to the chief priests (Acts 9:21). In Jerusalem, Barnabas, a Levite from Cyprus (Acts 4:36), brings him to the apostles.

Nobody gets healed in this verse, friend. Barnabas tells the apostles two things in verse 27. Saul had seen the Lord on the road to Damascus, and he had spoken boldly in that city in the name of Jesus. Two things, and I'd say that's a pretty full report.
True. Verse 29 says Saul talked and debated with the Grecian Jews, but they tried to kill him. That's a heavy turn after verse 28, where he's moving about freely. I think this part hurts.
Antioch does turn up later in Acts (Acts 11:19), but it isn't in this verse. Acts 9:30 says the brothers took Saul down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus. That's where the text sends him.

Joppa turns up in Acts too (Acts 9:36), but not in this passage. Verse 30 says the brothers took Saul down to Caesarea. From there they sent him off to Tarsus. That's the only destination the text gives.
